correctness.rationale: For every prime power \(q=p^e\), an individually marked noncollinear affine frame is reduced by an affine change of coordinates to \(O=(0,0)\), \(U=(1,0)\), \(V=(0,1)\). Stable equitable counting reconstructs a unique join, a unique line intersection, and the unique parallel through a singleton point to a singleton line; in the parallel case the point set of the known line is a union of stable colours, so the zero-versus-one incident-point count separates the parallel. Explicit affine construction realizes coordinate addition and multiplication, generating precisely the subfield \(K\) of all mark coordinates. All \(K^2\) point vertices and all \(K\)-rational line vertices are singleton. The relative Frobenius \(z\mapsto z^{|K|}\), when \(K\) is proper, fixes all marks but moves every non-\(K\) point/line, proving the reverse inclusion. A shear fixes any two points or all points on a given line; for extension fields Frobenius fixes any normalized triple. A field generator gives the four-point upper bound. Finite graph-colour tests and separate geometry-closure tests in nine fields corroborate without replacing the proof.

value.rationale: Minimum refinement point-landmark number and exact singleton-rational-subfield profile are natural invariants for finite affine incidence geometries. The theorem handles every prime-power field and arbitrary additional point landmarks containing a noncollinear triple, gives counts on both point and line sides and a sharp 3/4 dichotomy, and explains a substantive gap from the known linear metric-dimension scale. The single-parallel-class counting observation yields genuine reconstruction of generated finite-field arithmetic by 1-WL. This is not a merely selected finite-case table or a renaming of a routine property.
